This is out-and-back ground, so everything climbed here has to be reversed on tired legs.

waypoints.name: Thunder Creek Trailhead (Colonial Creek Campground, South Loop)
waypoints.note: This is a legitimately long/remote approach (24-mile round trip: Thunder Creek Trail to McAllister camp, off-trail to Borealis Lake, across Borealis Glacier to Lucky Pass)
waypoints.directions: Colonial Creek Campground sits on SR-20 at Diablo Lake, milepost 130, roughly 25 miles east of Marblemount. Turn in on the campground's south side and park in the large lot above the boat ramp, around 1,240 ft. That lot is also the Thunder Creek Trailhead, and the maintained Thunder Creek Trail runs south from it.

waypoints.name: Thunder Creek log crossing
waypoints.note: The original footbridge over Thunder Creek near mile 6.6 washed out in fall 2017; parties cross via a log felled about 1,000 ft downstream of the old bridge site. Coordinates approximate.

waypoints.name: McAllister Camp
waypoints.note: Backcountry stock camp where McAllister Creek meets Thunder Creek; leave the maintained trail here and pick up the unmaintained climbers' boot path at the first fork. Coordinates approximate.

waypoints.name: Ridge viewpoint
waypoints.note: Boot path up the north ridge passes a viewpoint here with the first views of Primus, Tricouni, and neighboring peaks. Coordinates approximate.

waypoints.name: Borealis Lake camp
waypoints.note: Standard base camp on a flat bench below the Borealis Glacier. Elevation and coordinates are approximate — not precisely surveyed.

waypoints.name: Lucky Pass (Primus-Tricouni col)
waypoints.note: Reached via roped travel across the Borealis Glacier's west edge, which has retreated and split into upper/lower tiers separated by slabs and cliffs. Elevation and coordinates are approximate.

waypoints.name: Goodell Creek / Upper Goodell Group Camp trailhead (SR-20, Newhalem)
waypoints.note: Unpaved turnout off SR-20 across from Newhalem, signed for Goodell Creek; NW Forest Pass and a self-issue wilderness permit (or WIC permit in Marblemount) required.
waypoints.directions: The trailhead is an unpaved turnout off SR-20 across from Newhalem, signed for Goodell Creek. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, along with a self-issue wilderness permit at the trailhead, or one from the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount if you plan to camp in the Terror or Crescent Creek basins.

waypoints.name: Upper trail fork
waypoints.note: Maintained forestry-road-bed trail ends here; climbers' path continues with diminishing cairns/flagging toward Terror Creek.

waypoints.name: Terror Creek crossing
waypoints.note: Ford Terror Creek at a shallow braid; crossing depth is very flow-dependent and can be a wade in high water.

waypoints.name: The Barrier
waypoints.note: Steep, brushy, loose ridge (spur off Mt. Degenhardt) separating Terror Creek and Crescent Creek basins; cross via a loose ledge system near the lower Terror Glacier or a higher moat crossing below Degenhardt — classic sustained 'Pickets Class 3' that turns parties back.

waypoints.name: Crescent Creek Basin camp (below Mt. Terror)
waypoints.note: Established high camp on a flat bench below Mount Terror with meltwater from two overhead slab streams; the basin runs 6,050–6,440 ft.

waypoints.name: Eye Col gully traverse
waypoints.note: Drop ~300 ft below the moraine to Crescent Creek's head, then rising-traverse below the Eye Col gully past an adjacent buttress on a minor rib to a notch, avoiding a closed chimney and loose choss.

waypoints.name: West Twin Needle
waypoints.note: Final class 5.7 pitch through larger chockstones/a narrow crack above the col, then class 2-3 scrambling under white slabs to the true summit; descend via rappels off the Himmelhorn–West Twin Needle col.

waypoints.name: Hannegan Pass Trailhead
waypoints.note: Same trailhead. NPS trip account describes traversing Whatcom Peak's east side / 'Whatcom Glacier route' from Whatcom Pass (reached via Hannegan Pass Trailhead).
waypoints.directions: The trailhead is at the end of Ruth Creek Road (FR-32), which turns off the Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542), at about 3,100 feet.

waypoints.name: Hannegan Pass
waypoints.note: High point of the maintained Hannegan Pass Trail; the route leaves good tread here and drops steeply into the Chilliwack River valley toward the Brush Creek approach.

waypoints.name: Chilliwack River ford
waypoints.note: Unbridged ford of the Chilliwack River reported thigh-deep at typical mid-summer flow; can run much higher and more dangerous during snowmelt or after rain.

waypoints.name: Graybeal Camp
waypoints.note: Established camp about 2 miles up the Brush Creek Trail; the camp itself is dry by late summer, so fill water bottles at Brush Creek roughly a half mile before arriving.

waypoints.name: Whatcom Pass
waypoints.note: Trail high point and standard base-camp area for the climb; junction with the Tapto Lakes path and the climbers' route onto the Whatcom Glacier.

waypoints.name: Whatcom Glacier traverse
waypoints.note: Traverse the east side of the retreating Whatcom Glacier around 5,200-5,500 ft; NPS warns of icefall and crevasse hazard here, worsening after mid-summer as the ice has thinned.

waypoints.name: Whatcom Peak
waypoints.note: [Coordinate corrected 2026-08-19: the stored pin sat 677 m away at 6752 ft, 822 ft from this peak's 7574 ft. Replaced with the peak's own coordinate, which the ground reads at 7509 ft.]

waypoints.name: Dose Forks
waypoints.note: West Fork Dosewallips Trail splits off the main Dosewallips Trail here at the river confluence; reliable water and a designated camp with toilet and bear wires.

waypoints.name: Diamond Meadows Camp
waypoints.note: Last established backcountry camp before Honeymoon Meadows; river-adjacent water source, elevation estimated by interpolating between Dose Forks and Honeymoon Meadows.

waypoints.name: Honeymoon Meadows Camp
waypoints.note: Forested backcountry campsite just below the actual meadows, the standard base camp for the White Mountain scramble day, at about mile 15.

waypoints.name: Anderson Pass
waypoints.note: Divide between the Quinault and Dosewallips drainages and trail junction toward Anderson Glacier; leave the maintained trail here and head south toward White Mountain — little to no water at the pass itself.

waypoints.name: Heather/scree slopes below the summit ridge
waypoints.note: Steep heather and talus that often retains hard, unmarked snow patches into midsummer; carry an ice axe and expect route-finding on this class 2 terrain.

waypoints.name: Dosewallips Road Washout / Current Vehicle Road End (near Elkhorn Camp)
waypoints.note: From this road-end, the route continues via bike/foot up West Fork Dosewallips River to Honeymoon Meadows before the Class 2 scramble to White Mountain's summit.

waypoints.name: Whiskey Bend Trailhead
waypoints.note: Start of the Elwha River Trail; Olympic Hot Springs Road is washed out beyond Madison Falls, adding roughly 6.9 mi of walking or biking each way just to reach this trailhead.

waypoints.name: Mary's Falls Camp
waypoints.note: Established riverside camp with reliable water from the Elwha River, roughly the halfway point to Hayes River.

waypoints.name: Hayes River Guard Station
waypoints.note: Historic patrol cabin and backcountry camp beside the Elwha River; the maintained trail continues upvalley toward Chicago Camp and Low Divide from here.

waypoints.name: Camp Wilder
waypoints.note: Backcountry camp (tent sites, bear wire, shelter) about 3.7 mi past Hayes River; leave the maintained trail here per route beta and head cross-country toward the upper Elwha Basin.

waypoints.name: Upper Elwha Basin
waypoints.note: Open heather benches and headwater creeks below Mount Wilder's south face; the last reliable water before the scree/talus climb to the ridge.

waypoints.name: South-Face Scree/Talus Slope
waypoints.note: Loose scree and talus on a slope that gains nearly 3,800 ft in under 2 miles on this south aspect; watch for rockfall and keep the party close together.

waypoints.name: Mount Wilder Summit
waypoints.note: True summit via the Class 2 south ridge; the southernmost peak of the Bailey Range, with Mount Olympus visible 8.7 mi WNW.
